children: Analysts expect AI data‑center demand to boost NVIDIA (NVDA) revenue, citing strong year‑over‑year growth and broad adoption of its AI chips, including Blackwell, by major cloud customers.
NVIDIA (NVDA): Analysts say approval for large Chinese firms to buy NVIDIA advanced chips could boost demand beyond prior guidance, since China was previously excluded from sales assumptions.
NVIDIA (NVDA) launched the Open Agent Safety Platform: OpenShell enforces runtime limits for AI agents; Sentry uses BlueField hardware to monitor and isolate or shut down misbehaving agents.
NVIDIA (NVDA) holds over $160B in cash, securities and receivables. Liabilities rose modestly with higher activity. Liquidity supports funding for buybacks and operations.
NVIDIA limited H200 AI chip shipments to mainland China in August. Company said older chips underperform Blackwell and China-related revenue fell year over year in Q1.
NVIDIA agreed to guarantee up to $105 billion to support land, power and shell buildout for an Ohio data center leased by an OpenAI affiliate; Goldman Sachs is involved in financing.
NVIDIA lobbied the White House and Commerce officials to oppose or alter China-focused chip export limits and tracking rules tied to NDAA proposals and AI-related export controls.
NVIDIA (NVDA) expanded AI infrastructure financing with major asset managers, supporting deals to mobilize vast third‑party capital and guaranteeing leases tied to an OpenAI data center project.
NVIDIA (NVDA): forward P/E ~24.8x, trailing P/E ~28.9x, PEG ~0.48 — high multiple supported by expected growth.
NVIDIA (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang met with White House officials on AI policy, signed AI safety accords, and is joining a meeting with top tech CEOs to discuss AI safeguards and voluntary reviews.
